newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR SIGNS FOR SARACENS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR SIGNS FOR SARACENS.

text.p: Springbok World Cup captain Francois Pienaar, unceremoniously dumped from South Africa's squad last month, has become the latest big-name player to sign for ambitious London club Saracens.

Pienaar, 29, will team up with the world's leading pointscorer Michael Lynagh and Frenchman Philippe Sella, the most capped test player in history, following the latest bold initiative by Saracens' millionaire backer Nigel Wray.

The blond flanker will find himself playing in front of around 6,000 spectators at the north London club's ground rather than the 60,000 audience which witnessed the World Cup triumph 18 months ago when President Nelson Mandela, wore a replica of Pienaar's No 6 jersey.
Pienaar was stretchered off the field in his 29th and possibly final test against New Zealand in Cape Town earlier this year. He was ignored by coach Andre Markgraaff for the current tour of France.
Pienaar has signed a two-contract and is expected to make his debut early in the New Year, but denied he was turning his back on the Springboks.
"I am determined to challenge for my place back in the South African national team and eventually go back home and put something back into South African rugby," he said.

Pienaar's leadership qualities have never been in doubt since he was chosen to captain South Africa on his test debut against France in Durban in 1993, having guided Transvaal to their first Currie Cup success for 21 years.

A law graduate, he has not always been universally popular outside his home province and World Cup euphoria turned somewhat sour when he led a walk-out of top Transvaal players over pay and came close to being sacked.
Even so, there was an outcry when he was jettisoned from the Springbok tour party with the captaincy passing to Gary Teichmann.
